Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

MacroFilters 0.2.2

Bug fixes

  • xts and zoo inputs now get the same defaults as the equivalent ts. The frequency is read from a regular Date, POSIXct, yearqtr or yearmon index. Before, a Date-indexed series had no frequency: hp_filter(), bhp_filter() and hamilton_filter() warned and assumed quarterly, while mbh_filter() (for d = "auto") and the "auto" bootstrap block size treated it as annual.
  • The "auto" bootstrap block size now follows the freq argument when x is a plain numeric vector. Before, it was always 2 for such vectors. A vector without freq still gets a block of 2.
  • zoo objects of class zooreg, which is what zoo::as.zoo() returns for a ts, are now accepted. Before, they were rejected as an unsupported class.
  • Multi-column input (mts, a multi-column xts or zoo, or a matrix) is now an error. Before, a multi-column xts or zoo was silently flattened into one long series. A single-column matrix is accepted as a vector.
  • autoplot() now draws xts and zoo input against its own time index: a date axis for a Date or POSIXct index, decimal time for yearqtr or yearmon. Before, it plotted the positions 1..n.

New features

  • hamilton_filter() and mbh_filter() gain a freq argument, as hp_filter() and bhp_filter() already had. It is used only when x carries no frequency of its own. A freq that contradicts the frequency of x is now ignored with a warning instead of silently.
  • All filters store in meta$freq the frequency read from x or freq, or NA when it is unknown.
  • All filters store in meta$na_lead the number of leading positions with no estimate: h + p - 1 for hamilton_filter(), 0 for the others.

Other changes

  • mbh_filter() no longer prints the calibrated Huber threshold when d = "auto". The value is in meta$d; set options(MacroFilters.verbose = TRUE) to get the message back.

Documentation

  • The package description no longer claims an automated diagnostic stage for unit roots and structural breaks, which the package does not have.
  • The README example used a us_gdp_xts object that the package does not ship. It now uses us_gdp_vintage from 2000 onwards.
  • The BIC formula in the bhp_filter() help now uses the trace of the boosted smoother, tr(B_m), which is what the code computes.
  • The mbh_filter() help announces that select_mstop will be deprecated in 0.3.0.

Internal changes

  • All four filters now build their result through one constructor, which derives the cycle as data - trend and validates the object. The checks are now ones that can fail: equal lengths, a finite trend outside the NA lead-in, and well-formed bootstrap bands. The old check of trend + cycle == data held by construction. The cycle of bhp_filter() and hamilton_filter() can change in the last floating-point digit; the trend and the bands do not change.
  • Removed the unused restore_class() helpers.
  • hp_filter() and bhp_filter() factor the HP system once and reuse it for the fit and the bootstrap.
  • Dropped the unused strucchange and usethis from Suggests, added mFilter to Suggests for a reference test, and set minimum versions for data.table, ggplot2 and Matrix.

MacroFilters 0.2.1

CRAN release: 2026-06-11

Other changes

  • mbh_filter()’s automatic knot count is now capped at 250 (min(max(20, floor(n / 2)), 250)). Series of 500 observations or fewer are unaffected; the cap only bounds the B-spline basis for long or high-frequency inputs, where extra knots inflate memory and runtime without adding flexibility (in a P-spline the difference penalty, not the knot count, controls smoothness).

Documentation

  • Corrected the MBH parameter tables in the Introduction vignette: the d = "auto" default is calibrated from the MAD of the HP cyclical residual (not first differences), and the default learning rate is nu = 0.1.
  • Fixed the COVID-19 highlight in the Introduction cycle plot, which was anchored to stale fixed indices instead of the 2020 date window.

MacroFilters 0.2.0

New features

  • Confidence bands via block bootstrap for all four filters (hp_filter(), hamilton_filter(), bhp_filter(), mbh_filter()). The new boot_iter and block_size arguments add $trend_lower / $trend_upper to the result: a 95% normal-approximation band (trend ± 1.96 * sd) built from a Circular Block Bootstrap of the cycle, with each replicate refit by the same estimator as the base fit.
  • New autoplot() method for macrofilter objects (ggplot2): draws the observed series, the estimated trend, and the confidence ribbon when present, with the time axis reconstructed from the stored temporal identity.
  • mbh_filter() gains hp_lambda to control the HP-based auto-calibration of the Huber threshold d when the input is a plain numeric vector whose true frequency is not annual.

Performance

  • The HP system matrix is now Cholesky-factorized once and reused across every bootstrap replicate (and every bHP inner iteration), instead of being re-factorized on each solve. This markedly speeds up hp_filter() and bhp_filter() with boot_iter > 0 (and the base bHP fit), with bit-identical results.

Other changes

  • The d = "auto" calibration in mbh_filter() now uses the MAD of the HP cyclical residual (output-gap scale) instead of mad(diff(y)), and reports the chosen value via a message().
  • Filters now return a list of class c("macrofilter", "list") and store the temporal identity (meta$ts_class, meta$tsp, meta$idx) so trend, cycle and bands can all be mapped back to dates for plotting.

Documentation

  • New vignette Uncertainty Bands via Block Bootstrap covering boot_iter, block_size, the end-point fan and the Hamilton conditional band.
  • mbh_filter() documents the mstop–d interaction (reducing mstop on long log-level series under-smooths the trend); hamilton_filter() documents the conditional bootstrap band behaviour.
